architecture_decisions: Project repository coverage and runtime token scope are separate authority layers.
work_items: Project repository coverage and runtime token scope are separate authority layers.
validations: Project repository coverage and runtime token scope are separate authority layers.

AC-01: validate protected requirement — For a Project bound to `github:<owner>/<repo>`, Parallax can determine before source mutation whether the approved GitHub App / Connect installation covers that exact repository.

AC-02: validate protected requirement — If the repository is not covered, Parallax returns `REPOSITORY_AUTHORIZATION_REQUIRED` and no source mutation occurs. Parallax does not silently broaden installation coverage.

AC-03: validate protected requirement — When repository coverage exists, Vercel Connect issues a short-lived GitHub credential requested for exactly the Project repository, and Parallax independently verifies the resulting credential is scoped to exactly that repository.

AC-04: validate protected requirement — An explicitly owner-approved installation may cover more than one repository, but a runtime credential requested for Project A cannot read or mutate Project B's repository and fails scope verification if it can see more than the requested repository.
AC-05: validate protected requirement — The current `Ryan9876/parallax` delivery path remains green and production preflight continues to verify exact derived-token repository scope.
AC-06: validate protected requirement — No PAT, reusable GitHub installation token, Supabase secret, QA password, service-role credential, or broad runtime bearer is introduced or persisted.

AC-07: validate protected requirement — After exact production deployment and required provider consent for `Ryan9876/sickbeard`, Engineering Run `a3a32343-507a-4384-a9bd-2fddaa0ce7fc` retries from PLAN without `CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE` or `REPOSITORY_AUTHORIZATION_REQUIRED` and durably advances beyond revision 1. Any later independent failure is recorded separately.

AC-08: validate protected requirement — The same authenticated QA-owned canonical run must advance beyond the former missing-static-target PLAN failure with no `source_bootstrap_failed` caused by static Vercel target registration or missing GitHub repository authority before #377 may close.

AC-09: validate protected requirement — Removing repository coverage or revoking the GitHub App / Connect installation causes subsequent readiness/token exchange to fail closed without reusing cached or persisted credentials.

AC-10: validate protected requirement — Provider readiness decisions record non-secret evidence sufficient to identify Project, canonical repository, readiness result, and provider-side installation/connector identity where safe, while excluding raw credentials and tokens.
risks: Project repository coverage and runtime token scope are separate authority layers.

critique:
:
- Repository coverage and runtime token scope are separate authority layers.
- A Project may proceed to source bootstrap only when its exact canonical GitHub repository is covered by an approved Parallax GitHub App / Vercel Connect installation.
- Runtime source credentials remain short-lived and exact-one-repository scoped through Vercel Connect `authorizationDetails`; broader installation coverage must never imply a broad runtime bearer token.
- Parallax must verify the derived GitHub credential sees exactly the Project repository before any source read or mutation.
- If installation coverage is absent, Parallax fails before Engineering Runtime source mutation with a typed, durable `REPOSITORY_AUTHORIZATION_REQUIRED` readiness state rather than a generic PLAN-time `CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE` failure.
- Project onboarding/readiness may expose a provider-consent action that authorizes the exact repository or a user-chosen broader installation scope.
- Parallax itself may not silently broaden GitHub App installation coverage.
- A user may deliberately choose a one-time GitHub App installation scope that covers all repositories Parallax is allowed to manage. Even under that broader…
